findings.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — downsize` is called with `from == to` (`tempfile.path` for both), so a failed or partial `convert`/`gifsicle` invocation can truncate/corrupt the only copy of the image in place; since the failure is never surfaced, a corrupted (possibly near-zero-byte) tempfile can pass the `tempfile.size > max` check and be handed to `Upload.create_for` as if it succeeded

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:69 — After the `while` loop exits (whether by success or by exhausting all 5 attempts), the code proceeds unconditionally to `Upload.create_for`/`upload.errors.empty?` with no re-check or error added when the image still exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so the size limit can be silently bypassed for images that can't be shrunk enough in 5 iterations

app/models/optimized_image.rb:145 — def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is immediately shadowed by the redefinition at line 149 (same method name, different arity), making it dead/unreachable code at class-load time; any future or external caller still using the old 4-positional-arg convention would silently break because `max_height` would land in the `opts` hash position

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is gated in `optimize` by `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but `from` here is `tempfile.path` (the multipart upload's temp file path), which typically does not retain the original `.gif` extension; as a result the animated/gifsicle code path is unlikely to ever trigger, so large animated GIFs get auto-downsized via the ImageMagick `convert ...[0]...` instructions instead, which select only the first frame and silently strip the animation

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL downloads are now capped at a hardcoded `10.megabytes` instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, while the downsize loop two lines below still compares against the real `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`; if the admin configures a limit above 10MB, oversized-but-allowed images are truncated/rejected by the download step before the new auto-downsize logic ever runs, and non-image API uploads no longer respect the configured max at all

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side size validation now hardcodes `10 * 1024` KB instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so per-type limits (e.g. avatar vs. composer image) and any admin-configured value other than 10MB are ignored, letting oversized files (or files that should be allowed) pass/fail the client check incorrectly relative to the server's actual configured limits

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 error handler hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`, so the "file too large" message shown to the user reports the wrong limit whenever the admin's real setting differs from 10MB

app/models/optimized_image.rb:161 — The `convert`/`gifsicle` shell invocation has no timeout, so a large or adversarial image that causes ImageMagick to hang can block the calling web worker indefinitely, compounding the worker-exhaustion risk from running this synchronously in the request path

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — FileHelper.download` for API uploads is now hardcoded to `10.megabytes` regardless of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, removing the admin-configurable cap and allowing larger downloads/memory and disk usage per upload than previously permitted

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Each loop iteration re-stats `tempfile.size` from disk after an in-place rewrite (from==to) rather than tracking size/dimensions in memory or checking progressively cheaper metrics, adding avoidable filesystem round-trips per attempt

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:72 — tempfile.size` is called unconditionally even though `tempfile` may be nil after the `rescue nil` on line 55 swallowed a download error, so a failed download raises an unhandled NoMethodError instead of a clean upload-failure response (and in the async `Scheduler::Defer` path the client never gets the already-sent success response corrected, leaving the UI hanging).

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` (false on ImageMagick failure) is never checked, so if the in-place conversion (from==to) fails or truncates the file, the loop keeps "retrying" on a possibly corrupted/zero-byte tempfile and can silently proceed to upload it with no logging or error surfaced.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — FileHelper.download(...) rescue nil` swallows all download exceptions (network errors, timeouts, malformed URLs) with no logging, and the diff raises the allowed download size to a fixed 10MB, widening the window for slow/failing downloads to be silently discarded with zero operational visibility.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:145 — Two `def self.downsize` are defined with different arities (4-arg width/height vs 3-arg dimensions); Ruby silently keeps only the second, making the first dead code, and this shipped with zero test coverage anywhere in the repo to catch the collision

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63 — The new auto-downsize retry loop (5 attempts, 80% shrink, calls OptimizedImage.downsize) has no spec exercising it at all, so a regression like the downsize signature collision above would silently pass CI

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:69 — No test specifies the behavior when the image still exceeds SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb after 5 downsize attempts; the loop just exits and Upload.create_for proceeds with an oversized tempfile, effectively bypassing the size limit, and this edge case is unverified

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — checkImageDimensions/upload size check now hardcodes 10MB instead of reading Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'], so admin-configured max_image_size_kb (and per-type limits) are silently ignored client-side, with no JS test asserting the setting is respected

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 error handler hardcodes 10MB instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, so the error message shown to users can be wrong when the admin lowers/raises the real limit, and no test covers this display logic

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — downsize` is called with `from == to` (`tempfile.path` for both), so a failed or partial `convert`/`gifsicle` invocation can truncate/corrupt the only copy of the image in place; since the failure is never surfaced, a corrupted (possibly near-zero-byte) tempfile can pass the `tempfile.size > max` check and be handed to `Upload.create_for` as if it succeeded

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`, i.e. `from == to`, so the only tempfile is modified in-place. In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` runs the conversion via a shell command and only returns `false` on non-zero exit status; the controller never checks that return value, so a failed/partial conversion would not be detected and `Upload.create_for(...)` would still be called with whatever bytes remain in the tempfile. The diff shows no post-conversion validation (size/type) before upload creation, making corruption/truncation a real risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:69 — After the `while` loop exits (whether by success or by exhausting all 5 attempts), the code proceeds unconditionally to `Upload.create_for`/`upload.errors.empty?` with no re-check or error added when the image still exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so the size limit can be silently bypassed for images that can't be shrunk enough in 5 iterations

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a downsize loop in `create_upload` that tries up to 5 times to reduce an oversized image, but after the loop it proceeds directly to `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` with no explicit post-condition check that `tempfile.size <= SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` and no controller-level error/response if downsizing never gets under the limit. Whether this becomes an actual bypass depends on validations inside `Upload.create_for`/model (not shown in the diff), so the “silently bypassed” part isn’t strictly verifiable here, but the missing re-check/clear failure handling is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is gated in `optimize` by `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but `from` here is `tempfile.path` (the multipart upload's temp file path), which typically does not retain the original `.gif` extension; as a result the animated/gifsicle code path is unlikely to ever trigger, so large animated GIFs get auto-downsized via the ImageMagick `convert ...[0]...` instructions instead, which select only the first frame and silently strip the animation

adjudication.rationale: In the new upload auto-downsizing loop, `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ..., allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` passes `from` as `tempfile.path`. But `OptimizedImage.optimize` only switches to the `_animated` instruction path when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true **and** `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Since a multipart tempfile path typically won’t end with `.gif`, the animated branch is likely never taken for animated GIF uploads, despite `allow_animation:` being set. This can lead to animated GIFs being processed by the non-animated downsize path, which (per existing design implied by `_animated` vs non-animated) risks stripping animation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes API URL downloads from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` (uploads_controller.rb:55). The new auto-downsize loop immediately below still uses `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` for its threshold, so if the configured max is >10MB, the download will still be capped at 10MB before the downsize logic can run. This also means API URL downloads no longer follow the configured `max_image_size_kb` limit (they are always limited to 10MB), diverging from prior behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:161 — The `convert`/`gifsicle` shell invocation has no timeout, so a large or adversarial image that causes ImageMagick to hang can block the calling web worker indefinitely, compounding the worker-exhaustion risk from running this synchronously in the request path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new synchronous loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` on potentially large user-provided images. In `OptimizedImage.convert_with`, the image processing is executed via a backtick shell call (`` `#{instructions.join(" ")} &> /dev/null` ``) with no timeout or other guard. If ImageMagick/gifsicle hangs on a crafted/degenerate image, the web request worker can block indefinitely, and the new loop can amplify that risk by invoking the command up to 5 times.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — FileHelper.download` for API uploads is now hardcoded to `10.megabytes` regardless of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, removing the admin-configurable cap and allowing larger downloads/memory and disk usage per upload than previously permitted

adjudication.rationale: The diff directly changes API URL uploads from `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` to `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` in `create_upload` (uploads_controller.rb). This hardcodes the download limit to 10MB regardless of the admin-configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so smaller configured caps no longer constrain server-side downloads, increasing potential per-request disk/memory/network usage (even though later downsizing may reduce the file after download).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Each loop iteration re-stats `tempfile.size` from disk after an in-place rewrite (from==to) rather than tracking size/dimensions in memory or checking progressively cheaper metrics, adding avoidable filesystem round-trips per attempt

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new loop repeatedly evaluates `tempfile.size` in the `while` condition (`while ... tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`) after calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`, which rewrites the file in-place (from==to). Each iteration will re-stat the tempfile on disk to get its size, which is a concrete, diff-grounded performance concern but not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:72 — tempfile.size` is called unconditionally even though `tempfile` may be nil after the `rescue nil` on line 55 swallowed a download error, so a failed download raises an unhandled NoMethodError instead of a clean upload-failure response (and in the async `Scheduler::Defer` path the client never gets the already-sent success response corrected, leaving the UI hanging).

adjudication.rationale: In `create_upload`, `tempfile` can be `nil` when `FileHelper.download(...) rescue nil` swallows a download error. While the newly added downsize block guards with `if tempfile && ...`, the subsequent call `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile, ..., tempfile.size, ...)` uses `tempfile` and `tempfile.size` unconditionally, so a failed download can raise `NoMethodError` rather than returning a clean upload failure. The async/UI-hanging part isn’t shown in the diff, but the nil-deref risk is directly supported by the code here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` (false on ImageMagick failure) is never checked, so if the in-place conversion (from==to) fails or truncates the file, the loop keeps "retrying" on a possibly corrupted/zero-byte tempfile and can silently proceed to upload it with no logging or error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` in-place and ignores its return value. In optimized_image.rb, `convert_with` returns `false` when ImageMagick fails, so a failure won’t be detected/logged. Because the loop condition is based only on `tempfile.size`, an in-place failed/truncating conversion could make the file size drop (even to 0), causing the loop to exit and the code to proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` with a corrupted/empty file.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `uploads_controller.rb` keeps `FileHelper.download(... ) rescue nil`, which will still swallow all exceptions with no logging/visibility, and it changes the download size limit from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a fixed `10.megabytes`. While not a directly provable functional defect from this diff alone (behavior depends on how `tempfile=nil` is handled later), it is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/operability concern made more impactful by the increased allowed download size.
